judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 3 (rank 2) Indicators in Strand 2: Reading, so direction rests on substantive content rather than coordinate gap. B3.2.2.1.3 (Sub-Strand 2: Phonics, under content standard 'Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write') asks learners to use basic elements of structural analysis (prefixes, suffixes, compound and root words) to decode unknown words — a word-recognition/morphological analysis skill. B3.2.6.1.2 (Sub-Strand 6: Vocabulary, under 'Understand word meanings and usage') takes the same morphological knowledge of prefixes and suffixes and applies it to interpret the meaning of unfamiliar words. The shared morpheme base plus the added semantic-inference step makes proficiency in the phonics-based structural decoding indicator supportive of success in the vocabulary meaning-interpretation indicator, so the developmental direction runs second-to-first rather than being mere repeated wording. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated (24 omitted items each) and the second endpoint's supporting LC metadata is truncated, and several ancestors carry merge/audit context; the judgment rests on the clean statement texts, codes, and identity scopes supplied.
